title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributes more than 51,000 appointment letters to the newly appointed youth in Government at 20th Rozgar Mela
subtitle:
India's Yuva Shakti is at the heart of our journey towards a Viksit Bharat.: PM

The Rozgar Mela reflects our commitment to creating new opportunities for the youth: PM

Our youth's talent and skills have earned global confidence; the world pins great hopes on our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our vibrant youth force: PM

Free Trade Agreements are unlocking new avenues of opportunity for our youth; these trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for our entrepreneurs, while creating fresh career possibilities for our youth: PM

India is currently the world's third-largest startup ecosystem; Moreover, India's startup story is no longer confined to major metropolitan areas, today, roughly half of all recognized startups are based in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 2:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various government organizations at the 20th Rozgar Mela today via video conferencing. Addressing on the occasion, he emphasized that this milestone brings immense joy to thousands of families, serving as a tribute to both the personal hard work of the candidates and the immense sacrifices made by their parents. "I wish you all the very best for this new beginning in life,” remarked Shri Modi.
Welcoming the new appointees into the Government of India as the nation marches toward the monumental milestone of a developed nation by 2047, the Prime Minister emphasized the pivotal role of youth in continuously empowering the twin campaigns of a developed and self-reliant India through every administrative decision. He highlighted their special responsibility toward fellow youth, noting that the talent and skills of the younger generation have captured the world's trust, fueling immense global expectations from Indian innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power."The world has high hopes from our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our youth power,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the recently concluded BRICS Summit, the Prime Minister stated that the administration’s strategy is to expand international cooperation far beyond traditional government-to-government interactions. He explained that initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal are designed to integrate entrepreneurs, farmers, women, and the youth directly into global partnerships. "Everyone should become an active participant in this partnership,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the economic diplomacy of the past few years, the Prime Minister pointed out that Free Trade Agreements with approximately 40 countries are unlocking unprecedented career possibilities. He emphasized that these agreements forge new markets and dynamic partnerships for domestic entrepreneurs while expanding career horizons for the youth. "These Free Trade Agreements are creating new doors of possibilities for our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the government's sustained focus on future-ready skilling, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the National Education Policy, the Skill India Mission, the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships. He highlighted the PM-SETU scheme, which is modernizing one thousand government ITIs with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees alongside direct industry participation. "Our endeavor is that the education and skills of the youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy,” asserted Shri Modi.
Praising the explosive growth of the domestic startup ecosystem, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's position as the world's third-largest startup hub, noting that nearly half of recognized startups now hail from tier-two and tier-three cities. He commended the youth from smaller towns for actively working on their ideas, building companies, and generating new employment opportunities for their peers. "Today the youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a major role in India's new economy,” observed Shri Modi.
Outlining the strategy to boost private sector employment, the Prime Minister highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana, a massive one lakh crore rupee initiative aiming to introduce two crore youths into the formal workforce for the first time. He detailed that the scheme offers up to 15,000 rupees in incentives for first-time employees while also financially rewarding employers who generate new jobs. "The government is working on every front to increase employment in the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Connecting job creation to robust macroeconomic health, the Prime Minister explained that new youth opportunities emerge only when the economy grows, investments increase, and new industries expand. He highlighted the nation's impressive 7.8 percent growth rate and a 12 percent surge in investments during the first quarter, noting that rating agencies are upgrading the nation's economic outlook despite pervasive global uncertainties. "The reforms of the past years have a major contribution behind this growth of India,” noted Shri Modi.
Directing the new officials to embrace an era of continuous administrative transformation, the Prime Minister stressed the critical need to simplify tax compliance, enhance the ease of doing business, implement reforms in education and skilling, and open new sectors to innovation. He tasked the young bureaucrats with ensuring that the momentum of governance improvements remains unstoppable throughout their tenures. "It is necessary that the Reform Express in the country runs continuously at full speed,” asserted Shri Modi.
Invoking his poetic remarks about claiming the sun, the sea, the boat, and the sailor to conquer the waves, the Prime Minister challenged the new recruits to match this courage by championing the deep aspirations of the country's youth. He insisted that every file signature and every administrative decision must actively clear hurdles, allow ideas to flourish, and promote innovation-driven investment that ultimately creates employment. "Your signature on every file should be one that advances youth aspirations,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Appealing to their personal journeys, the Prime Minister urged the fresh appointees to utilize their new authority within the government system with deep empathy. He advised them to actively dismantle the bureaucratic hurdles they themselves faced before joining the service. "Your effort should be that the difficulties you have gone through, other youths should not have to go through them,” remarked Shri Modi.
Encouraging a mindset of lifelong learning in a rapidly changing world, the Prime Minister directed the recruits to continuously upgrade their skills and master new technologies through the Mission Karmayogi framework. He noted that the 'Karmayogi Prarambh' module has been specifically designed to help new entrants navigate the system, joining the 1.7 crore employees already on the iGOT platform. "The more you improve yourself, the better you will be able to serve the citizens of the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that the true strength of any government lies in public trust, the Prime Minister reminded the recruits that their daily work, from processing elderly pensions to student scholarships and farmer subsidies, directly impacts common lives. He stressed that their behavior, efficiency, honesty, and sensitivity will ultimately define the citizen's personal experience with the state. "Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty, all this will determine what that citizen's experience with the government is like,” observed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with a powerful administrative mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the new officials to adopt the philosophy of 'Nagrik Devo Bhava' (The Citizen is Divine) in their daily service, equating citizen service to national service. He expressed his unwavering belief that they will fulfill their duties with utmost dedication and service across all departments. "Your success will be even greater when your work makes a citizen's life easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s remarks during 20th Rozgar Mela via video conferencing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My dear young companions,
The festive season has begun in the country. Amidst these celebrations, today brings a new joy into the lives of thousands of families. Today, more than 51,000 youth across the nation are receiving appointment letters for government service. Behind the achievement you have reached today is not only your hard work, but also the dedication of your parents and family members. I extend heartfelt congratulations to all of you and your families. I wish you all the best for this new beginning in life.
Friends,
Today you are joining the Government of India at a time when the nation is moving towards a very big goal - the goal of making India developed by 2047. In this, the role of youth like you is immense. While serving in government, you must take every decision that strengthens the campaign for a developed India and for self‑reliant India. As youth, you have a special responsibility towards other young people. You can see how the talent and skills of our youth have won the trust of the entire world. The world has great expectations from our innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power. Just a few days ago, the BRICS Summit concluded. India’s effort has been that BRICS cooperation should not remain limited to governments alone - our entrepreneurs, farmers, women, youth, everyone should become active participants in this partnership. With this vision, initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal have been launched.
Friends,
In recent years, India has signed free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries. These FTAs are opening new doors of opportunity for our youth. Such trade agreements create new partnerships for our entrepreneurs, open new markets, and create new career possibilities for our youth.
Friends,
In recent years, the Government of India has consistently focused on preparing youth for the future. The National Education Policy, Skill India Mission, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships - all aim to ensure that the education and skills of our youth align with the needs of a changing economy. One example is PM‑SETU. Through this scheme, with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees, 1,000 government ITIs are being modernized. Direct participation of industry has been ensured in this.
Friends,
Another picture of the strength of India’s youth is visible in our startup ecosystem. Today India is the world’s third‑largest startup ecosystem. And India’s startup story is no longer just about big cities. Today, nearly half of recognized startups are in tier‑two and tier‑three cities. That means youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a big role in India’s new economy. Our young people from smaller towns are working on their ideas, building new companies, and creating new employment opportunities for other youth as well.
Friends,
Our effort is that new employment opportunities also grow rapidly in the private sector. With this vision, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched. About 1 lakh crore rupees are being spent on this scheme. With its help, nearly 20 million youth will get the chance to join the workforce for the first time. Under this scheme, the government is giving an incentive of up to 15,000 rupees to youth who get their first job. Employers who create new jobs are also being encouraged by the government. That means the government is working on every front to increase employment in the country.
Friends,
New opportunities for youth are created only when the country’s economy grows, when investment increases, new industries are set up, and new sectors expand. Today India is one of the fastest‑growing major economies. In the first quarter of this financial year, India’s growth rate was 7.8 percent. Investment increased by nearly 12 percent. Rating agencies are upgrading India’s ratings. And this progress is happening at a time when the world is passing through many uncertainties. Behind India’s growth is the major contribution of reforms carried out in recent years. In your tenure, you must continue to accelerate reforms. Whether it is simplifying tax and compliance, increasing ease of doing business, reforms in education and skilling, opening new sectors for innovation, or ease of living - at every level, the Reform Express must continue at full speed. And as government employees, you will have a very big role in this in the present and coming years.
Friends,
I said a few days ago - the sun must be ours, the sea must be ours. The boat must be ours, the sailor must be ours. The courage to write victory on the waves must be ours. Today India’s youth are moving forward with this courage. Now, while serving in the Government of India, it is your responsibility to understand the aspirations of the country’s youth and fulfill your duties accordingly. I urge you again - every decision you take, every signature you put on a file, must advance the aspirations of youth. In your tenure, you must ensure that obstacles in the path of youth are removed, their ideas get opportunities to move forward, innovation increases investment, and investment creates new employment opportunities.
Friends,
Now you are becoming part of the government system yourselves. Therefore, your effort must be that the difficulties you faced, or that your parents faced, should not be faced by other youth. The hardships your parents endured, the hardships you may have endured - no citizen of our country should have to endure them anymore. This is the work you must do as soon as you enter the government system.
Friends,
Today, transformation is happening rapidly in every sector of the country. You have reached here by continuously learning. Now from here begins a new journey of continuous learning. You must keep improving your skills. You must understand new technologies and new systems. Mission Karmayogi helps you achieve this very purpose. More than 17 million government employees are connected to the iGOT Karmayogi platform today. And for new companions like you, Karmayogi Prarambh has been specially designed. The more you improve yourself, the better you will serve the citizens of the country.
Friends,
You must always remember one more thing. The real strength of government is the trust of the country’s citizens. Whatever ministry you are in, whatever department you are in, your work will touch the life of ordinary citizens in some way. A pension for an elderly person may move forward because of your work. A scholarship for a student may depend on your responsibility. A facility for a farmer may be delivered through your department. For some citizen, you may be the face of the government. Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty - all these will determine how that citizen experiences the government.
Therefore, friends,
In government service, our mantra must be - Citizen Devo Bhava, Citizen Devo Bhava. Service to citizens is service to the nation. Your success will be greater when your work makes life easier for a citizen. I am confident that wherever you are, in whichever department you are, you will continue to fulfill your duties with dedication and a spirit of service. Once again, I congratulate you all.
Thank you very much.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
subtitle:
India is showing how development and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand: PM

Often, the responsibility for carbon emissions has been unfairly placed on developing countries; However, the historical truth is that even today, India's contribution to per capita carbon emissions is less than half of the global average: PM

Over the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field and sector related to the environment; Our major focus has been on renewable energy, which has played a significant role in environmental protection: PM

Among the G-20, India is the only country to have met the commitments made at the COP-21 Summit in Paris ahead of time: PM

Our development is both speedy and sustainable: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 1:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” today at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation's profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers. “India is now providing solutions to modern climate challenges,” asserted Shri Modi.
Addressing the flawed global narrative regarding carbon footprints, the Prime Minister pointed out that developing nations are unjustly blamed, despite developed nations emitting up to six times more carbon per capita than India. He detailed how the nation uses international platforms to assert this historical truth and showcase its traditional environmental strengths, recalling the launch of the "Convenient Action- Continuity for Change" book at COP-21 and the creation of platforms like One Sun, One World, One Grid, the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Global Biofuel Alliance, and the International Big Cat Alliance. "We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Bridging ancient philosophy with modern execution, the Prime Minister detailed the extraordinary progress made across every environmental sector over the past dozen years, specifically highlighting a massive strategic pivot toward renewable energy. He proudly stated that the nation proudly occupies a unique position within the G-20 for having achieved its COP-21 commitments ahead of schedule, setting global benchmarks in non-fossil fuels and solar capacity. "India's performance on every parameter is a topic of discussion in the world today,” noted Shri Modi.
Presenting stark evidence of the nation's solar revolution, the Prime Minister cited the leap from a mere 2 gigawatts of capacity a dozen years ago to over 160 gigawatts today, fueled by the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana which has solarized over 50 lakh homes with financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. He added that 30 lakh farmers have received solar pumps under the Kusum Yojana, while the completed One Nation-One Grid project has successfully prevented 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions. "We have started a mission to make homes themselves the center of solar power generation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Expanding on the massive strides in the broader clean energy landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted the threefold increase in wind capacity, significant hydro expansions, and a newly energized focus on nuclear power generation that now welcomes private players. He noted that these combined efforts have nearly quadrupled the nation's non-fossil energy capacity while advancing cleaner technologies like Coal Gasification. "India has achieved major milestones in other sectors of clean energy as well,” noted Shri Modi.
Celebrating the dawn of advanced clean mobility, the Prime Minister proudly announced the recent launch of the country's first Hydrogen Train, which also holds the record as the world's longest. He described this technological leap as a foundational milestone for the future of green transportation. "This is the beginning of a new era of clean mobility,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the massive adoption of green vehicles, the Prime Minister highlighted a staggering 950-fold increase in Electric Vehicles, jumping from under three thousand sales before 2014 to roughly 25 lakh last year. He also pointed out that the modern FASTag system on highways and expressways has drastically reduced fuel wastage by minimizing wait times at toll booths. "India is embracing this opportunity of the EV revolution with full force,” noted Shri Modi.
Showcasing the sweeping modernization of public transport infrastructure, the Prime Minister contrasted the meager five-city, 250-kilometer metro network of 2014 with today's expansive system operating in over 20 cities. "India has joined the ranks of those countries in the world that have a metro network of more than a thousand kilometers,” asserted Shri Modi.
Underscoring the eco-friendly transformation of heavy logistics, the Prime Minister explained how the near-total electrification of the railways has saved crores of liters of diesel from being burned. He highlighted the massive environmental benefits of the newly inaugurated 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, where historic double-stack container trains are replacing hundreds of polluting trucks per journey. "You can imagine on what a large scale this is helping the environment,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing to alternative eco-friendly transport modes, the Prime Minister celebrated the operationalization of approximately 5,000 kilometers of inland waterways across the country. He explained that a single standard inland vessel navigating these routes can carry a load equivalent to dozens of trucks. "This too is providing great help in environmental conservation,” noted Shri Modi.
Summarizing the collective impact of these transit upgrades, the Prime Minister emphasized that the sweeping changes across the entire mobility sector serve as undeniable proof of the nation's balanced growth trajectory. He stated that rapid progress is entirely compatible with environmental preservation. "Our development is speedy as well as sustainable,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Praising the unprecedented mass participation in water conservation, the Prime Minister celebrated the construction of over 70,000 Amrit Sarovars and 1.5 crore rainwater harvesting structures under the Catch the Rain campaign. He noted that modern irrigation techniques under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and 'Per Drop, More Crop' are actively saving water for over 2 crore farmers. "Unprecedented work is being done on water conservation in India,” noted Shri Modi.
Championing the global revival of millets, the Prime Minister explained how promoting the cultivation of water-efficient Shree Anna has boosted domestic production and increased exports to 1.5 lakh tons, simultaneously creating economic opportunities and conserving water. He credited these relentless national efforts for inspiring the global celebration of 2023 as the International Year of Millets. "Because of this model, the world is also joining us,” remarked Shri Modi.'
Underscoring the massive scale of ecological agriculture, the Prime Minister detailed the establishment of 24,000 natural farming clusters across 12.5 lakh hectares under the National Mission on Natural Farming. He also highlighted the successful development of 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties and the strategic promotion of agro-forestry to reduce the national footprint. "By promoting agro-forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the comprehensive nature of the country's environmental efforts, the Prime Minister shared that the very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent over the last 12 years. He praised the ongoing 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign for inspiring citizens to plant crores of trees in a continuous, nationwide drive.
Addressing the critical challenge of plastic pollution, the Prime Minister reiterated the national ban on single-use plastics and the strong push toward a Circular Economy based on reducing, reusing, and recycling thousands of tons of daily waste. He cited the Gobardhan Yojana as a prime example of converting rural organic waste into valuable resources through a Wealth from Waste model. "Our endeavor is that instead of treating waste as a problem, it should be transformed into a resource,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Elevating the significance of the nation's environmental achievements, the Prime Minister stated that these robust statistics represent far more than domestic progress. He framed the nation's developmental data as monumental, direct contributions to the survival and prosperity of the entire human race. "These are also figures of India's contribution to the future of humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored the profound relationship between the earth and its inhabitants that drives these responsible actions. He concluded his address on an optimistic note, expressing deep confidence that the conference deliberations would yield innovative solutions, and offered his final felicitations. "India is also working to build a responsible and sustainable future,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address at the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 1:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Bhupender Yadav ji, Attorney General of India R. Venkataramani ji, National Green Tribunal (NGT) Chairman Justice Prakash Srivastava ji, all distinguished dignitaries present in this hall, ladies and gentlemen.
For centuries, India has guided the world on the subject of nature and environment. With that ideological commitment, and based on our cultural experiences, India is now also providing solutions to modern climate challenges, while at the same time calling for collective efforts of humanity. I am happy that this NGT conference is carrying forward that mission. For this event, I extend my congratulations and best wishes to all the officials of NGT and all dignitaries associated with it.
Friends,
We all know that often the responsibility for carbon emissions has been wrongly placed on developing countries. Many of my companions from the Global South are present here. But the historical truth is that even today, India’s per capita carbon emissions are less than half the global average. In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s. Six times higher. India presents this fact strongly on global platforms. And I say to every Indian - show your strength too. We have also presented our traditions and their power before the world. On these very subjects, during COP‑21 in Paris, we launched the book Convenient Action – Continuity for Change. We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along. Whether it is the vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid, or the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, Global Biofuel Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance, Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) - each of these platforms is becoming a stage for India’s dedicated commitments on climate and environment.
Friends,
Today’s India is moving forward by weaving its ancient ideas of environmental protection into a modern vision. In the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every sector related to the environment. Our major focus has been on renewable energy, and this has played a big role in environmental protection. India is the only country in the G20 - I say this before the big leaders of the G20 - the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about. On every parameter - non‑fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions - India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide. Look at the figures. Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts. Twelve years ago - 2 gigawatts. If there are lawyers here, please note these figures, they may come in handy. Today it has crossed 160 gigawatts. From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years. Under the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, we launched the mission to make homes themselves centers of solar power generation. Under this scheme, more than 5 million homes have already installed rooftop solar panels. This is more than the total number of homes in many countries. For this, the government has provided financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. Under the KUSUM scheme, the government has installed solar pumps in the fields of 3 million farmers. We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project. Not only this - LED bulbs in homes have proven successful in saving electricity. Crores of LED bulbs have been distributed to households. And the results of these efforts are before us today. From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.
Friends,
Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors. In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled. Hydropower capacity has increased significantly. And now the country is working rapidly on nuclear energy generation. Those who give long speeches on the environment - when I advance nuclear energy work, they will stand in the courts to stop it. A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector. Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled. India is also promoting technologies like coal gasification for cleaner use of coal.
Friends,
India is now working rapidly in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen. Just a few days ago, India’s first hydrogen train was launched - and it is the world’s longest hydrogen train. This marks the beginning of a new era of clean mobility.
Friends,
In 12 years, the number of electric vehicles in our country has increased nearly 950 times. 950 times. In the year before 2014, fewer than 3,000 EVs were sold in India. Last year, nearly 2.5 million EVs were sold in India. That means India is embracing the opportunity of the EV revolution with full strength, and this is also helping the environment. On our highways and expressways, modern fast‑track systems have reduced waiting at toll booths. This has stopped the fuel wastage that used to occur at toll booths.
Friends,
Until 2014, in five cities of our country there was less than 250 kilometers of metro network. Lawyers here should note this figure. Before 2014, only five cities had less than 250 kilometers. Today, metros run in more than 20 cities, and India has joined the countries with more than 1,000 kilometers of metro network.
Friends,
With nearly 100 percent electrification of railways, billions of liters of diesel burning has been avoided. The environment has been protected. Just this month, a 3,000‑kilometer‑long Dedicated Freight Corridor was inaugurated. Every train running on it carries loads equal to hundreds of trucks from one place to another. The operation of double‑stack container freight trains is historic in itself. You can imagine how greatly this helps the environment.
Friends,
Today, transportation is happening on about 5,000 kilometers of waterways in the country. This is the most environment‑friendly mobility. A standard inland vessel running on these waterways carries loads equal to dozens of trucks in one journey. This too is greatly helping environmental protection.
Friends,
All these changes in the mobility sector alone are proof that our development is both speedy and sustainable.
Friends,
Today, with the participation of millions of people, unprecedented work is happening in India on water conservation. I am happy that more than 70,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed in the country. Under the Catch the Rain campaign, nearly 15 million water harvesting structures have been built, preserving rainwater. Through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, more than 20 million farmers today are connected with modern irrigation facilities. Initiatives like Per Drop More Crop are also saving water. Shri Anna - that is, millets - are another great successful example. India is promoting the cultivation of millets, which consume less water. In recent years, millet production has increased in the country, and exports have risen to about 150,000 tonnes. This is creating new opportunities for farmers, while also saving water. And because of this model, the world is joining us. Thanks to India’s efforts, 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.
Friends,
Under the National Mission on Natural Farming, today about 1.25 million hectares in the country have developed 24,000 clusters of natural farming. Not only this, nearly 3,000 varieties of climate‑resilient crops have also been developed in the country. By promoting agro‑forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints.
Friends,
How wide‑ranging our efforts are can be seen in India’s forest coverage. This too I mention for my lawyer friends. In the past 12 years, our very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent. This is a very big achievement. Under the campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (One Tree in the Name of Mother), crores of trees have been planted across the country. And this campaign continues.
Friends,
Plastic waste has also been a major challenge for the environment. That is why India has banned single‑use plastic. With the mantra of reduce, reuse, and recycle, we have promoted the circular economy. Today, thousands of tonnes of waste are being recycled every day in India. Through the Gobardhan Yojana, cow dung and other organic waste in villages are being converted into useful resources. Our effort is that waste should not be seen as a problem, but transformed into a resource under the Waste to Wealth model.
Friends,
All these figures are not just India’s development statistics - they are India’s contributions for the future of humanity.
Friends,
Our cultural thought is - “Mata bhumih, putro aham prithivyah” - meaning, this earth is our mother and we are her children. With this thinking, India is working to build a responsible and sustainable future. I am confident that the discussions in this conference, and the new ideas and solutions that emerge from it, may become a great support for future generations. Once again, I extend my many best wishes to all of you for this conference. Thank you very much.

title: Ministry of Ayush Advances Artificial Intelligence for Ayurveda and Traditional Medicine
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Building on the digital foundation laid by Ayush Grid, the Ministry of Ayush is now advancing Artificial Intelligence as the next frontier for Ayurveda and the wider Ayush sector. The Ministry has been exploring AI across healthcare, research, education, information services and investment facilitation, with an emerging ecosystem that includes both specialised AI applications and broader collaborations with national AI initiatives.
At the citizen-facing level, the MAISP Chatbot is designed to make Ayush-related information, including Ayurveda, readily accessible through a conversational interface. The ARP Research Assistant, a GenAI-based assistant, extends the Ayush Research Portal, helping researchers navigate Ayurveda and other Ayush literature more effectively. The eLMS Chatbot introduces AI-based Student Life Cycle Management for Ayurveda and other Ayush education institutions, while the e-CHARAK Chatbot functions as a medicinal-plant trade assistant, connecting conversational AI with the ecosystem that underpins Ayurvedic pharmacology. Yoga Saarthi serves as a yoga recommendation AI chatbot, and Nivesh Saarthi serves as an AI assistant for investment in the Ayush sector. Together, these chatbots demonstrate the expansion of Ayush Grid from digital portals towards interactive, intelligent and user-oriented AI services.
At the IndiaAI Impact Summit 2026, the AI Impact Casebook on Health, developed in partnership with the World Health Organization, featured a dedicated snapshot from the Ministry of Ayush titled "AI-driven Decision Support for Ayurveda: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Approach." The inclusion of this Ayurveda use case in a global health AI casebook underscores the potential of Generative AI and RAG to strengthen evidence-based Ayurvedic knowledge and the wider digital transformation of traditional medicine.
The Ministry's broader AI ecosystem is being advanced through participation in the IndiaAI Innovation Challenge, with a focus on developing AI-enabled solutions tailored to the Ayush sector. Key use cases include voice-based Electronic Health Records, disease-trend detection, and personalised treatment-support solutions, aimed at leveraging Artificial Intelligence to enhance healthcare delivery, clinical insights and patient-centric care across Ayurveda and other Ayush systems.
On 11 July 2025, the WHO, ITU and WIPO jointly released a technical brief, Mapping the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Traditional Medicine, examining how AI can support traditional medicine while highlighting the importance of responsible, evidence-informed and culturally appropriate approaches, including for Ayurveda.
The Ministry of Ayush has collaborated with IndiaAI and the Digital India Bhashini Division (DIBD), MeitY, creating opportunities to explore artificial intelligence, language technologies, digital health and advanced computing for the Ayush ecosystem. Ministry artefacts are now available on AI Kosh to support wider AI research and dissemination in the Ayush and Ayurveda domains. Through the Bhashini collaboration, Ayush Grid portals, including those serving Ayurveda practitioners, students and citizens, are now available in 22 scheduled languages of India, enabling wider participation and reach across the country's linguistic diversity.
With AI assistants alongside collaborations involving IndiaAI and Bhashini, the Ayush ecosystem is moving further towards intelligent and citizen-centric digital services. The intent is not to replace traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with technology, but to use Artificial Intelligence to strengthen, connect and amplify that knowledge, making it more discoverable, evidence-based and accessible to citizens in India and around the world.

content:
As India moving towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, reliable and sustainable power holds the key for national growth. Navigating the dual imperative of uncompromised baseload energy and ambitious decarbonisation,
NLC India Limited (NLCIL)
—a Navratna enterprise under the Ministry of Coal
with existing power generation capacity of 8,405 MW and Mining Capacity of 59.10 MTPA
at present—is redefining its identity from a legacy mining enterprise to rapidly evolving into an integrated, future-ready energy powerhouse backing India's
Panchamrit
climate goals.
Energy Security:
Reliable energy is critical to economic expansion, and coal and lignite continue to serve as the nation's baseload anchor. To meet India's power requirements sustainably, NLCIL is expanding its mining footprint responsibly while modernizing generation:
Capacity Scaling:
Increasing total mining capacity from 59.1 MTPA to 104.35 MTPA by 2030, targeting 115.85 MTPA by 2047 to avoid import dependence.
High-Efficiency, Low-Emission (HELE) Generation:
Transitioning to cleaner thermal power with supercritical units at Ghatampur (1,980 MW) and ultra-supercritical pit-head thermal power projects at Talabira (2,400 MW) and Machhakatta (4,000 MW), drastically minimizing specific coal consumption and emissions.
Logistical Efficiency via FMC:
Commissioning 63.5 MTPA capacity across First Mile Connectivity (FMC) rail corridors at Pachwara South, North Dhadu (west), Talabira, Machhakatta and New Patrapara (South) to eliminate road transport emissions/ oil dependency, thus improving logistical efficiency.
Renewable Energy:
NLCIL is actively developing India's clean energy through its dedicated green arm,
NLCIL Renewables Limited (NIRL)
:
10 GW by 2030:
Growing its operational renewable portfolio from ~1.8 GW to over 10 GW by 2030 (scaling to 32.7 GW by 2047), establishing a 50% clean energy mix in its generation well ahead of schedule.
Battery Energy Storage System (BESS):
Projects under development includes 250 MW / 500 MWh in Tamil Nadu, 300 MW / 1,800 MWh with SECI in Rajasthan, 275 MW  / 550 MWh with GUVNL in Gujarat and 50 MW / 200 MWh with WBSEDL.
Pumped Storage Projects (PSP):
Targeting large-scale storage assets in Tamil Nadu and Odisha to balance renewable grid intermittency.
Other Diversification Projects:
To safeguard India from global supply chain disruptions and to achieve low-carbon industrialization, NLCIL is implementing the following:
Green Hydrogen & CCS:
Constructing a pilot 4 MW solar-powered PEM electrolyzer Green Hydrogen plant at Neyveli and partnering with IIT Madras on advanced Carbon Capture Systems.
Strategic Mineral Autonomy:
Currently, NLCIL has secured domestic composite exploration licenses for phosphorite, limestone in Chhattisgarh and vanadium, titanium in Telangana states. Also pursuing international prospects through KABIL for critical minerals.
By aligning with national self-reliance (
Aatmanirbhar Bharat
), NLC India Limited is ensuring Nation’s energy security today, while laying a robust foundation for low carbon emission revenue businesses/ initiatives for tomorrow.

title: Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Addresses Rozgar Mela in Chennai
subtitle:
Dr Pemmasani Exhorts New Recruits to identify challenges faced by citizens and explore solutions through technology, innovation and entrepreneurship

Union MoS Highlights India’s transformation in manufacturing, infrastructure, digital governance and telecom connectivity since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi

More than 51,000 candidates receive appointment letters across the country under the nationwide Rozgar Mela
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, while addressing the 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai today, congratulated the newly appointed government employees and their families, calling upon the recruits to approach public service with integrity, empathy, responsibility and a commitment to continuous learning.
Dr. Pemmasani said the occasion marked an important milestone not only for the recruits but also for their families, who had supported them through examinations and the recruitment process. He said securing a government job remains an important aspiration for many young Indians and congratulated the recruits selected from among more than 51,000 candidates receiving appointment letters across the country under the nationwide Rozgar Mela.
With the completion of the 20th Rozgar Mela, around 12.75 lakh young people will have received appointment letters through the initiative.
Sharing his journey from a modest family background to becoming a doctor, entrepreneur and public representative, Dr. Pemmasani emphasised the importance of learning, adaptability and perseverance. He encouraged the newly appointed employees to seek guidance from experienced colleagues and make effective use of digital learning resources and AI tools.
The Union Minister of State urged the recruits to remain open to new postings, languages, cultures and working environments, saying that exposure to unfamiliar surroundings can help build confidence and broaden their understanding of the country.
Emphasising the human dimension of government service, Dr. Pemmasani said employees should not allow routine administrative work to diminish their sense of purpose. A government employee may view a file as routine administrative work, but for the citizen concerned, it could represent an important aspect of their life.
The Union MoS urged the recruits to question established practices, verify facts and avoid blindly following processes simply because they are widely followed. “Just because 100 people do the wrong thing, that doesn’t make it a right thing,” he said, emphasising the importance of integrity and sound decision-making.
Speaking about India’s transformation since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi , Dr. Pemmasani highlighted the changes in governance, infrastructure, technology and public service delivery. He said India’s mobile manufacturing ecosystem has expanded from just two manufacturing units in 2014-15 to around 300 today. Mobile phone production has also increased substantially.
The Minister of State said the transformation is equally visible in infrastructure. The national highway network has expanded significantly. Railway electrification has progressed rapidly. Vande Bharat trains and railway station redevelopment are improving connectivity and passenger experience.
He also highlighted the growth of indigenous defence production. India’s defence exports have increased from around ₹600 crore in 2013-14 to around ₹30,000 crore in 2025-26.
Furthermore, the Minister of State encouraged the young employees to identify challenges faced by citizens and explore solutions through technology, innovation and entrepreneurship.
Towards the conclusion of his address, Dr. Pemmasani outlined three things for the recruits to remember throughout their careers: the citizen, their families and their younger selves. He said these principles would help them remain grounded and committed to public service. Looking towards 2047, he urged the newly appointed employees to continuously reflect on whether they are living up to the trust placed in them by the country, their families and the citizens they serve.
Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani concluded his address by congratulating the newly appointed employees and wishing them success in their careers and service to the nation.

title: Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol addresses the inauguration ceremony of the new Head Office of Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society Limited in Belagavi, Karnataka
subtitle:
​​​​​​​Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the cooperative sector of the country is continuously getting strengthened: Shri Murlidhar Mohol

More than 160 important decisions have been taken in the cooperative sector under the leadership of Shri Amit Shah; work worth approximately Rs 3,000 crore has been initiated for computerisation of nearly 80,000 PACS: Shri Mohol

Nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions have joined the three national-level Multi-State Cooperative Societies; village-level cooperative institutions have been linked with more than 25 types of business activities

Cooperative banking is gaining new strength through the Umbrella Organisation for Urban Cooperative Banks and the ‘Sahkar Sarathi’ platform for Rural Cooperative Banks

Cooperative sector will require approximately 17 lakh trained human resources over the next 10 years; ‘Tribhuvan’ Sahkari University is an important initiative in this direction: Shri Mohol

New initiatives such as White Revolution, Sahkar Bima and Bharat Taxi are continuously expanding the scope of cooperation: Shri Mohol

Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society has approximately 4.60 lakh members, 263 branches across the country and a business of more than Rs 9,000 crore
date:
Posted On:
                19 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, continuous efforts are being made to strengthen, modernise, make transparent and expand the cooperative sector of the country. In this sequence, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol today addressed the inauguration ceremony of the new Head Office of Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society Limited (Multi-State), located at Nandi in Chikodi Taluka of Belagavi district, Karnataka. Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi, several dignitaries from the State of Karnataka, representatives of the cooperative sector and a large number of citizens were present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that today is an extremely important and joyous day for the cooperative sector in Karnataka. Shri Mohol conveyed his best wishes to the entire team of the institution on behalf of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah and the Union Ministry of Cooperation.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society has approximately 4.60 lakh members, its 263 branches are spread across the country and the Society has a business of more than Rs 9,000 crore. He said that today also marks the 36th Foundation Day of the institution. He congratulated the entire team of the institution for managing cooperative activities on such a large scale.
Shri Mohol said that cooperation has expanded on a large scale in States such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. He said that Shri Annasaheb Jolle and his wife have made an important contribution to the cooperative sector of Karnataka. Referring to the work carried out by them in various areas, including cooperative sugar factories, cooperative banks and credit societies, Shri Mohol appreciated their contribution.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji deserves appreciation for giving a new direction to the cooperative system of the country. He said that today more than 8.5 lakh cooperative societies and cooperative institutions are functioning in the country and approximately 32 crore people are members of these cooperative institutions. Nearly 20 to 25 crore families are directly connected with cooperation and, thus, almost half of the country’s population is associated with the cooperative system in one form or another.
Shri Mohol said that earlier, the work relating to cooperation in the country was handled under a department of the agriculture sector within the jurisdiction of a Joint Secretary. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, recognising the scale and importance of the cooperative sector, established an independent Ministry of Cooperation in the country. He said that over the last nearly five years, the cooperative sector of the country has undergone a fundamental transformation under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah.
Shri Mohol said that Shri Amit Shah has vast experience of working across the cooperative banking system, from village societies to district banks and State-level cooperative banks. Under his leadership as the country’s first Minister of Cooperation, cooperation in India received a new momentum and work began towards its equitable expansion and development across the country.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that more than 160 important decisions have been taken for the cooperative sector during the tenure of Shri Amit Shah. He said that through these decisions, efforts have been made to strengthen and empower the cooperative movement of the country. Work worth approximately Rs 3,000 crore has been initiated for the computerisation of nearly 80,000 village-level Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS). In addition, village cooperative institutions have been linked with 25 different types of businesses to expand their economic activities and sources of income.
Shri Mohol said that three Multi-State Cooperative Societies have been created with the objective of developing a comprehensive cooperative ecosystem for farmers and nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions across the country have joined them as members. He said that through this, work is being undertaken to provide new opportunities to farmers and cooperative institutions.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that there are more than 1,500 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Earlier, there was no common organisation to understand the difficulties and problems faced by these banks, address issues related to the Reserve Bank of India and facilitate their business operations. He said that for this purpose, an Umbrella Organisation, NUCFDC, has been established in the country, through which assistance is being provided to ensure the smooth functioning of Urban Cooperative Banks.
Shri Mohol said that an independent platform named ‘Sahkar Sarathi’ has been developed for Rural Cooperative Banks. He said that keeping future requirements in mind, there is a need to take cooperation to every part of the country, further expand its reach, make the functioning of cooperative institutions more systematic and efficient, and further strengthen trust and credibility in the cooperative system.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that approximately 17 lakh people will need to be trained to work in the cooperative sector over the next nearly 10 years. He said that with this objective, the country’s first cooperative university, ‘Tribhuvan’ Sahkari University, has been launched, which will play an important role in developing trained human resources for the cooperative sector.
Shri Mohol said that renewed work has also begun in the field of the White Revolution. Along with this, several new initiatives such as Sahkar Bima and Bharat Taxi have been launched under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. He said that through these initiatives, the cooperative sector of the country is continuously becoming stronger.
The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation, referring to the role of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), said that NCDC provides assistance and financial support to cooperative institutions across the country. He underlined the importance of NCDC in providing financial and institutional support to cooperative institutions. Shri Mohol expressed confidence that the cooperative movement would continue to progress in the same manner throughShri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society. He said that such cooperative institutions have an important role in truly realising and fulfilling the resolve of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’.

title: SEMICON India 2026 Concludes Successfully, Showcasing India’s Growing Role in the Global Semiconductor Ecosystem
subtitle:
Three-day event records more than 51,000 registrations and cumulative around 40,000 footfall; over 600 exhibitors, including participation from around 300 international companies

Representatives from 52 countries, 6 Country Pavilions and 12 State Pavilions bring together the global and domestic semiconductor ecosystem

56 MoUs / announcements and strategic initiatives across three days strengthen collaborations in design, manufacturing, packaging, materials, equipment, R&D, startups and talent
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 10:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of India’s flagship semiconductor conference, concluded successfully today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, marking another step in the development of India’s semiconductor ecosystem. Held from 17–19 September 2026 under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem,” the event featured over 600 exhibitors, including around 300 international participants, representatives from 52 countries, and over 150 speakers. Six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State Pavilions, a Startup Pavilion, Workforce Development Zone, Innovation Showcase & Student Hackathon, showcased different dimensions of the semiconductor value chain. The event recorded 51,656 total registrations and cumulative footfall of about 40,000.
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 and highlighted India’s progression from policy discussions and project planning to commercial semiconductor production. He interacted with young chip designers and students and virtually inaugurated commercial production lines at CDIL Semiconductor, Mohali, and Suchi Semicon, Surat, taking the number of operational commercial semiconductor units among the 12 projects approved under Semicon 1.0, to five. The Prime Minister also outlined the transition to Semicon 2.0, aimed at developing capabilities across the semiconductor value chain. Semicon 2.0 has an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore and is structured around six pillars - design, machines and materials, new fabs, advanced packaging, research and talent development.
The three days witnessed 56 MoUs, announcements and strategic initiatives, spanning semiconductor design, fabrication, advanced packaging, equipment and materials, power electronics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), High-Performance Computing (HPC), Research and Development (R&D), logistics, technology commercialisation, skilling and workforce development. Major announcements during the event included collaborations and investment plans involving semiconductor manufacturers, equipment and materials companies, design firms, academic institutions and skilling organisations.
Day 2 focused on translating the semiconductor mission into wider ecosystem development. Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways, and Information & Broadcasting, outlined the implementation approach for Semicon 2.0, with emphasis on design, machines and materials, fabs, advanced packaging, applied R&D and talent. Deliberations during the day covered resilient supply chains, AI-enabled chip design and manufacturing, advanced packaging, indigenous R&D, power electronics, display technologies, workforce development and women’s participation in semiconductor manufacturing. The discussions reflected the need to build not only fabrication capacity but the wider ecosystem of equipment, materials, gases, chemicals, precision manufacturing, intellectual property and skilled manpower required for a globally integrated semiconductor industry.
The concluding day focused on technological capability, industry collaboration, ease of doing business, sustainability, displays, workforce development and deep-tech startups. Discussions highlighted the need to strengthen scientific knowledge, materials, manufacturing know-how, research and talent alongside physical capacity. The Leadership Forum, moderated by Shri Amitesh Kumar Sinha, CEO, India Semiconductor Mission and Additional Secretary, MeitY, emphasised a coordinated “Silicon to Systems” approach linking semiconductor design and manufacturing with materials, equipment, packaging and electronics systems. Shri Sushil Pal, Joint Secretary, MeitY, moderated discussions on investment facilitation and ease of doing business, while other sessions covered sustainable manufacturing, advanced displays, deeper localisation and industry-ready skills across the semiconductor value chain.
The concluding day also placed strong emphasis on indigenous innovation and deep-tech entrepreneurship. Discussions examined ways to connect semiconductor research and intellectual property with procurement, patient capital, manufacturing and markets. The Digital India RISC-V Grand Challenge under the Chips to Startup Programme attracted 1,236 teams comprising 5,045 participants, with awards presented to top-performing teams for solutions developed using indigenous VEGA and SHAKTI processor-based System-on-Chips. The concluding programme also recognised Startup Pitch and Hackathon winners, reinforcing engagement among startups, students, investors and industry to support technology commercialisation and innovation. Three hackathons organised by KLA, Synopsys and Lam Research in partnership with CeNSE-IISc witnessed over 3,800 team registrations from more than 900 colleges, providing students opportunities to address industry-relevant semiconductor challenges. Winners were recognised through cash prizes, internships, software tools and compute credits.
International engagement remained a key feature across all three days through six Country Roundtables. On Day 1, the India–USA Roundtable brought together 180 participants, while the India–Japan Roundtable witnessed participation of 200 participants, with discussions focused on commercial partnerships, technology collaboration, equipment and materials, resilient supply chains and R&D. On Day 2, the India–Singapore Roundtable brought together 142 participants, the India–Europe Roundtable 139 participants, and the India–South Korea Roundtable 115 participants, advancing cooperation in manufacturing, advanced packaging, equipment and materials, investment, R&D and talent. On Day 3, the India–Malaysia Roundtable brought together around 150 participants, focusing on leveraging Malaysia’s established back-end semiconductor capabilities and India’s strengths in design, engineering and manufacturing to deepen partnerships across OSAT, advanced packaging, materials, equipment, supply chains and talent.
Across its three days, SEMICON India 2026 brought together the complete “Silicon to Systems” journey - design and intellectual property, materials and equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging, electronics manufacturing, R&D, startups, sustainability and talent. The scale of the 2026 edition represented a substantial expansion over SEMICON India 2025. With more than 600 exhibitors, around 300 international companies, participation from 52 countries, and 56 MoUs, announcements and strategic initiatives, SEMICON India 2026 provided a platform for investment, technology partnerships, commercialisation of research, industry–academia collaboration, startup development, skilling and international cooperation across the semiconductor value chain.

title: SEMICON India 2026 concludes with focus on indigenous innovation, sovereign computing and semiconductor talent development
subtitle:
Concluding session features 15 announcements spanning RISC-V innovation, AI and quantum platforms, fab automation, start-up engagement and workforce development

Digital India RISC-V Grand Challenge under C2S Programme awarded to three teams for solutions built on indigenous processors
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 10:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
SEMICON India 2026 concluded today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, with a series of 15 announcements and collaborations during its concluding session. The initiatives are aimed at strengthening India’s capabilities in semiconductor design, indigenous computing, fabrication management, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, start-up engagement and workforce development. They brought together Government institutions, industry, academia and skilling organisations to translate India’s semiconductor ambitions into deployable technologies, stronger domestic infrastructure and industry-ready talent.
The day’s proceedings placed particular emphasis on innovation using indigenous processor platforms, wider access to advanced computing, sovereign digital infrastructure and practical skilling across chip design, verification, testing, semiconductor manufacturing and Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP).
1. Digital India RISC-V Grand Challenge winners announced
The winners of the Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Grand Challenge, organised by Maker Village under the Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), were announced. The challenge received participation from 1,236 teams comprising 5,045 participants from across the country. Three teams received total prize money of Rs 60 lakh:
First Prize
: Meevisai Technologies Pvt. Ltd., representing Team Digital Dawgs from SASTRA University, Thanjavur, developed an autonomous water-surface cleaning robot, using the indigenous SHAKTI processor developed by IIT Madras. The robot is designed to clean inland water bodies such as ponds and temple tanks.
Second Prize
: Digiscope LLP, representing Team Binary Bandits from ER&DCI Institute of Technology, Thiruvananthapuram, developed VEGA Chikitsa, a digital stethoscope that captures heart and lung sounds with real-time filtering and supports recording, remote monitoring and machine-learning-assisted murmur screening, using the indigenous VEGA processor developed by CDAC.
Third Prize
:
Zetawave Technologies Pvt. Ltd., representing Team NeuroBytes from the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, developed a forest-environment monitoring system using the indigenous VEGA processor.
New technology platforms and innovation challenges launched
2.
Bharat AI-SoC Challenge 2026–27:
The second edition of the challenge was launched under the C2S Programme for undergraduate and postgraduate students and working professionals in artificial intelligence and system-on-chip design. The initiative is supported by the UK Government through the UK-India Technology Security Initiative and will remain open for one month from the date of launch.
3.
SCL DMIS for fab automation:
The Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL), Mohali, launched Device Manufacturing Integrated System (DMIS), an indigenous manufacturing execution system for efficient management of wafer-fabrication activities. Its modular, plug-and-play architecture supports end-to-end management from order booking and wafer fabrication to final packaging, strengthening shop-floor control and manufacturing efficiency.
Partnerships for sovereign computing and digital infrastructure
4.
C-DAC and NLC India Limited:
The organisations announced a collaboration to establish a data centre within India’s energy-sector ecosystem by leveraging indigenous technologies and expertise. The partnership seeks to promote secure and advanced digital infrastructure while strengthening self-reliance and technological capability in the energy sector.
5.
C-DAC and Bharat Electronics Limited:
C-DAC and Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) announced a collaboration to jointly develop and deliver indigenous high-performance computing, artificial intelligence and sovereign data-centre solutions. The partnership will combine C-DAC’s advanced computing technologies with BEL’s system-integration and deployment capabilities.
Indigenous AI and quantum platforms
6.
PARAM Vidya:
C-DAC launched PARAM Vidya, a ready-to-deploy AI Excellence Lab-in-a-Box for universities, research institutions, start-ups and MSMEs. Its plug-and-play architecture and indigenous software ecosystem are intended to widen access to artificial intelligence and high-performance computing and support research, skilling and application development.
7.
PARAM Shavak-QS:
C-DAC inaugurated PARAM Shavak-QS, a compact, high-performance quantum simulation platform designed to enable research, education and innovation in quantum technologies and broaden access to quantum-computing capabilities.
Industry-aligned semiconductor workforce initiatives
8.
Electronics Sector Skills Council of India and Maitrio Labs:
A strategic partnership was announced to strengthen the semiconductor skilling ecosystem and develop training infrastructure aligned with the emerging requirements of semiconductor manufacturing.
9.
Electronics Sector Skills Council of India and Truechip Solutions:
The organisations announced a partnership for training and certification of youth in semiconductor circuit design, verification and testing, with the objective of building industry-ready skills across the semiconductor value chain.
10.
SEMI and Peachtree Elevate:
An MoU was exchanged to advance semiconductor workforce development through technical training, professional education and customised certification pathways, combining SEMI’s global ecosystem and SEMI University resources with Peachtree Elevate’s demand-led skilling model.
11.
NIELIT semiconductor workforce initiatives:
NIELIT announced initiatives for ATMP skilling and a Digital Twin for Semiconductor Manufacturing. These will combine digital learning, hands-on training and immersive simulations through NIELIT Centres of Excellence, the NIELIT Digital University Platform, the upcoming ATMP facility at Guwahati and the Digital Twin.
12.
Ramaiah Institute of Advanced Skills and Technology (RIASAT) and IISc Bengaluru:
The Ramaiah Institute of Advanced Skills and Technology and IISc Bengaluru exchanged an MoU to advance India’s semiconductor capabilities through closer institutional collaboration.
Innovation start-up engagement and ecosystem roadmap
13.
SEMICON India Hackathon Grand Finale:
The SEMICON India Hackathon received 3,808 team registrations from 881 colleges and 1,053 ideas, with 10 teams reaching the Grand Finale. Teams from VIT Vellore and IIT Madras emerged as winners, while teams from KPR Institute and VIT Vellore were runners-up.
14.
Startup Mitra:
Under Startup Mitra, 11 start-ups pitched to over 20 venture capital investors. Elphins Technologies secured first place, Meukron Technologies  stood second, while Multi Nano Sense Technologies and CraftifAI jointly received third place.
15.
EY and ISEA report launch:
EY and the India Semiconductor and Electronics Association (ISEA) launched the report “Semicon India 2.0: From Capacity Creation to Ecosystem Leadership”. The report highlights an opportunity for India’s semiconductor market to grow from nearly USD 64 billion in 2026 to USD 200 billion by 2035 and outlines a roadmap to translate domestic demand and design talent into leadership across manufacturing, advanced packaging and innovation.
The announcements at the concluding session complemented the MoUs and partnerships unveiled during the first two days of SEMICON India 2026. Together, they reflected a broad-based effort to strengthen the ecosystem from indigenous processors and research platforms to fabrication operations, sovereign infrastructure, industry-academia collaboration and specialized talent.
Together with the 41 announcements and MoUs during the first two days, the initiatives at SEMICON India 2026 reflected increasing collaboration among Government, industry, academia, startups and R&D organisations to translate semiconductor capabilities into technology development, skilled talent, commercialisation and deployment.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ in New Delhi; Releases NGT Mobile Application
subtitle:
Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav underscores India’s commitment to Climate Action anchored in Equity, Implementation and Sustainable Development

Two-day Conference brings together Global Stakeholders to deliberate on Collaborative Action on Pressing Global Environmental and Climate Challenges
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 SEP 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the National Green Tribunal’s (NGT) two-day International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, in New Delhi today. The inaugural session was graced by Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, Attorney General for India Shri R. Venkataramani, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav and Chairperson, National Green Tribunal, Justice Prakash Shrivastava.
Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation's profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers.
(Link:
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2312353&reg=48&lang=1
)
Delivering his inaugural remarks, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant highlighted India’s longstanding environmental jurisprudence, noting that the Supreme Court has, over the decades, recognised the right to a pollution-free environment as a fundamental right and developed principles including the precautionary principle, polluter pays principle, absolute liability and public trust doctrine. The Chief Justice said Indian climate jurisprudence has brought climate-related rights into sharper constitutional focus, recognising that adverse effects of climate change can implicate fundamental rights relating to equality, livelihood and health. He called for collective judicial wisdom, scientific knowledge and international cooperation to strengthen global environmental stewardship.
Addressing the august gathering, Shri Bhupender Yadav highlighted India’s climate commitments under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, noting that non-fossil sources now account for 54.18 per cent of installed electricity capacity, surpassing the 2030 target of 50 per cent nine years ahead of schedule. He said India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity and is the world’s second-largest solar growth market, demonstrating that economic growth and climate action can advance together.
Shri Yadav also highlighted India’s achievements in wildlife and ecosystem conservation, from the successful Cheetah reintroduction programme and conservation breeding programme of the Great Indian Bustard to the conservation and restoration of woodlands, grasslands and wetlands. He said India’s forest and tree cover has reached 8.27 lakh square kilometres and quoted the Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 by the UN FAO, according to which India has retained its third position globally in terms of annual net forest-area gain. Looking ahead to UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, he said India will continue to advocate climate action centred on equity, implementation and the needs of vulnerable countries.
The Union Minister said that forums bringing together judges, policymakers, scientists, practitioners and experts from across the world are vital at a time when environmental challenges transcend national boundaries. He emphasised that the choice before the world is not between development and environment, but between sustainable development and development that cannot be sustained. The Minister said India’s approach to environmental responsibility is rooted in its civilisational ethos, which views the Earth as a shared inheritance and a sacred trust, and reaffirmed India’s commitment to collective action towards a sustainable, resilient and just future.
In his speech, Attorney General for India Shri R. Venkataramani said that no country can address the environmental challenge alone and that global action must move beyond declarations towards practical and enforceable mechanisms. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call that “global action must match global ambitions”, he said India can set examples through the balancing path it has chosen while pursuing development and environmental protection. He called for a new global environmental regulatory framework and stronger international institutions to address environmental justice, while integrating concerns relating to energy and food security, housing, health, water, ecosystems and economic opportunities.
Welcoming the delegates earlier, NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava highlighted India’s comprehensive approach to environmental governance under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He said that India's initiatives demonstrate the country's commitment not only to national action but also to global environmental cooperation. Justice Shrivastava said the initiatives reflect a larger vision of a cleaner, greener, more resilient and sustainable India. He emphasised that environmental protection is not the responsibility of any one institution or sector, but a collective national and global responsibility, with the consequences of environmental degradation often falling most severely on those least responsible for them.
The Prime Minister also launched the National Green Tribunal (NGT) Mobile Application during the inaugural session of the conference.
The two-day Conference is bringing together jurists, academicians, policymakers, scientists, environmental experts and other stakeholders from 17 countries across the world, along with international organisations United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and Asian Development Bank (ADB). The event focuses on dialogue, knowledge exchange on judicial, scientific, policy and institutional best practices, while encouraging collaborative action on pressing environmental and climate challenges.
The Conference features four technical sessions covering key aspects of environmental and climate governance, two of which were held today.
Technical Session-I
- ‘Climate Justice, Equity and Inclusion: From Principles to Action’ - focused on equity and inclusion in climate action, environmental and social safeguards, and the interconnected impacts of climate change and environmental degradation.
Technical Session-II
- ‘The Future of Environmental Law and Governance’ - discussed strengthening institutions and enforcement mechanisms, sustainable and liveable cities, energy transition, green infrastructure and green finance.
The Conference seeks to strengthen environmental law and institutions, advance climate justice and inter-generational equity, promote sustainable and resilient cities, facilitate a just energy transition and foster collaborative action on transboundary environmental challenges. It also focused on sharing research, best practices and innovative solutions, building partnerships, and developing actionable recommendations and a roadmap for future cooperation.
